questions: Is the child difficult or impossible to awaken during these episodes?
Does the child stop responding to your voice or touch during an episode?
Do the eyes repeatedly roll upward or become fixed to one side?
Does the child have stiffening, rhythmic jerking, or repeated twitching of the limbs or face?
Does the child stop breathing, turn blue, or become unusually pale during an episode?
Has an episode lasted longer than five minutes?
Has the child had more than one similar episode?
Does the child return completely to normal after each episode?
Does the child currently have a fever?
Has the child recently had vomiting, diarrhea, poor feeding, excessive sleepiness, or unusual irritability?
Has the child recently fallen or sustained a head injury?
Has the child taken any medication or been exposed to someone else’s medication, especially an anti-nausea or antipsychotic medicine?
Could the child have swallowed or been exposed to a poisonous substance?
Has the child ever had seizures or similar abnormal movements before?
Has the child had any loss of previously acquired developmental skills?
Was the child born prematurely or with complications affecting breathing or the brain?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Joubert syndrome (Joubert-related neurodevelopmental disorder), an autosomal-recessive ciliopathy causing cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and the molar-tooth brainstem malformation; the causative gene cannot be specified without genetic testing.

Alternative 1: COACH syndrome (Joubert syndrome with hepatic fibrosis), not supported by currently normal liver tests.

Alternative 2: Poretti–Boltshauser syndrome due to biallelic LAMA1 variants.

Alternative 3: Another Joubert-related ciliopathy, such as an AHI1-, TMEM138-, or CEP290-associated disorder.
